title: Inspector General Officer (I) (Col to 2ndLt) FMOS, IGMC
raw_text:
21.     MOS 8049, Inspector General Officer (I) (Col to 2ndLt) FMOS, IGMC

    a. Summary. Inspector General (IG) Officers promote Marine Corps
institutional effectiveness, efficiency, discipline, morale, and combat
readiness through impartial and independent inspections, assessments,
investigations, and training. They are responsible for all credible
complaints of fraud, waste, abuse of authority, and mismanagement. IG
Officers are integral to the Marine Corps Inspector General Program that is
composed of the Inspector General of the Marine Corps (IGMC), Command
Inspectors General (CIGs), and their respective staff. IG Officers act in an
independent and professional manner, without command influence, pressure, or
fear of retaliation from any level within the Marine Corps. IG Officers have
acquired subject matter expertise in IG functions through personal experience
and formal training. They are currently serving, or have served, in an IG-
related billet during their career. IG Officers have also received
certification from the Office of the Inspector General of the Marine Corps
(IGMC) validating that they have achieved competency in accomplishing IG
functions and responsibilities as outlined in MCO 5430.1, such as
facilitating an IG hotline program, managing an IG inspections program, and
providing oversight to Marine Corps organizations.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must not have been relieved for cause from an IG billet.

            (2) Must pass an initial IGMC records screen for assignment to an IG
billet.

        (3) Security requirement:        must possess an active secret security
clearance.




                                          1-319                        Enclosure (1)
 1144                                                                 NAVMC 1200.1L




       c.   Requirements

            (1) Complete the IGMC 101 Course (SSC-0AV).

        (2) Complete the IGMC Advanced Course via mobile training team or
virtual training team (SSC-0AW).

        (3) Assigned to a billet for a minimum of 6 months at IGMC or a CIG
office directly performing IG duties and responsibilities as outlined in the
most recent version of MCO 5430.1.

            (4) The certifying authority for this MOS is the IGMC.

       d.   Duties

        (1) Provide independent and impartial oversight of unit functions in
order to sustain a high level of institutional readiness across the Service
and prevent fraud, waste, abuse, and mismanagement.

        (2) Facilitate the execution of IG-related programs, such as
assistance and hotline, inspections, investigations, intelligence oversight,
and analysis and evaluations.

        (3) Provide feedback to unit command teams regarding program trends,
inefficiencies, and recommendations.

        (4) Report the state of unit effectiveness, efficiency, discipline,
economy, ethics, integrity, and readiness to command teams.

        (5) Become an expert on IG functions and responsibilities and advise
both unit commanders and staff on IG-related matters.

    e.      Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
None.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
